transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

At work my mind jumps to every little thing going on around me, and I lose track of what I’m doing in the middle of a customer call. It's gotten so bad lately that I'm really worried about losing my job.
Did these attention problems start in childhood, or did they begin only recently after a specific stressor or life change?

They’ve gotten much worse over the last two years since my work switched to a fast-paced new system, but looking back, I've actually had these issues since childhood. Even in elementary school, my teachers had to move my seat because I wouldn't stop talking or tapping my pencil, and my report cards always said I was smart but rushed and made careless mistakes.
Do you still have symptoms of hyperactivity or impulsivity now, such as feeling restless, fidgeting, interrupting others, or acting before thinking?

Yes, absolutely. I'm constantly jiggling my leg or clicking my pen, and sitting still in meetings makes me feel this buzzing inside like I'm trapped and need to pace. I also keep catching myself interrupting coworkers or finishing their sentences because the thoughts just pop out of my mouth before I can stop them.
Do these attention, restlessness, or impulsive symptoms cause problems in more than one area of your life, such as at work, at home, or in relationships?

Yes, they definitely affect both my work and my home life. At work, I'm currently on a performance improvement plan and risk losing my job because of constant documentation errors. At home, I forget bills and leave chores unfinished, which forces my wife to pick up the slack and has caused a lot of stress and tension between us.
Before age 12, were these attention, hyperactivity, or impulsive symptoms already present in more than one setting, like both at school and at home?

Yes, they were definitely a major issue at school, where teachers constantly moved my seat because I wouldn't stop talking or tapping my pencil, and my report cards always said I was smart but careless. I mostly remember those school-related struggles quite clearly, though. I'm not as certain about the specific details of how it affected things at home from that far back.

Do you remember having similar problems with attention, hyperactivity, or impulsivity at home before age 12, such as being unable to sit still, forgetting instructions, or getting in trouble for acting without thinking?

I honestly don't remember too many specifics about how it was at home back then, but I definitely had these issues as a kid. In elementary school, my teachers were constantly moving my seat because I wouldn't stop talking, tapping my pencil, or staring out the window instead of finishing worksheets. My report cards always noted that I was smart but "doesn't pay attention" and "rushes and makes careless mistakes."

Did these attention, hyperactivity, or impulsive symptoms also cause problems at home before age 12, such as forgetting instructions, being unable to sit still, or getting in trouble for acting without thinking?

I'm really not sure or can't recall specific problems at home from that far back. I just vividly remember the issues at school, like my teachers constantly moving my seat and my report cards saying I rushed and made careless mistakes.

I'm really not sure and don't clearly recall having those specific problems at home or with friends before age 12. I mostly just remember the issues being pointed out by my teachers at school, like when I would tap my pencil or stare out the window.
